Demo walkthrough

Placing, cancelling, and recovering an order

A step-by-step tour of the saga-orchestrated order processing system running locally in Docker — the order list, a single order's step history, the Retry and Mark Shipped actions, and two orders watched live from submission to resolution.

In progress Placed Shipped Cancelled Needs attention
Stack: docker compose (mysql, redis, coordinator, 4 step services, notification-service, angular frontend) Frontend: localhost:4200 API: localhost:3000

Two bugs found and fixed while producing this walkthrough

  1. Retry compensation silently threw. The undo processor records a business-level failure (e.g. SIMULATED_COMPENSATION_FAILURE) without throwing, so BullMQ marks that job completed, not failed. retryCompensation() called existingJob.retry('failed') unconditionally, which throws Job ... is not in the failed state whenever the underlying failure was business-level rather than a transport error. Fixed by checking the job's actual state and re-queuing a fresh job when it isn't literally failed.
  2. A resolved retry never left "Needs attention." Even once the undo genuinely succeeded, decideCompensationOutcome() only updated the saga row WHERE status = 'IN_PROGRESS' — but by the time a retry resolves it, the row is already NEEDS_ATTENTION, so the update matched nothing and the status stayed stuck forever. Fixed by allowing the transition from either state. Step 6 below shows the corrected behavior: the order actually flips to Cancelled after Retry.

Run it yourself

cp .env.example .env
docker compose up --build

curl -F file=@orders_bulk.csv http://localhost:3000/api/csv/upload

Walkthrough

Nine steps, start to finish

Step 1

The order list — status, steps done, paging

2,500 orders loaded from orders_bulk.csv. Each row shows its status badge, a chip per saga step (green once DONE), and the list paginates 20 at a time.

localhost:4200/orders
Step 2

Filtering by status

The status dropdown narrows the list to one state at a time — here, filtered to Placed.

localhost:4200/orders?status=PLACED
Step 3 → 4

Order detail, then Mark Shipped

Opening ORD002498 shows all four saga steps DONE. Clicking Mark Shipped flips the badge to Shipped and pushes an event to the notification service.

localhost:4200/orders/ORD002498
before — Placed
localhost:4200/orders/ORD002498
after clicking "Mark Shipped"

Notification service log, moments later: Notification sent for shipped order ORD002498

Step 5

A cancelled order — the undo trail

ORD002499 had CHARGE_PAYMENT fail on the way in. The step history shows both phases: the three DO steps that ran before the failure, and the UNDO steps that reversed them.

localhost:4200/orders?status=CANCELLED
localhost:4200/orders/ORD002499
Step 6

Needs attention, then Retry

ORD001911 got stuck mid-compensation: its CREATE_ORDER undo failed and stayed failed. After clearing the simulated condition (the same recovery move the coordinator's own e2e test makes — fixing the underlying cause out-of-band), clicking Retry compensation re-runs just that one undo step.

localhost:4200/orders/ORD001911
before — Needs attention, CREATE_ORDER undo FAILED
localhost:4200/orders/ORD001911
after "Retry compensation" — resolved to Cancelled
localhost:4200/orders?status=NEEDS_ATTENTION
Step 7

Watching a fresh order get placed, live

Submitted directly against the coordinator API, then opened immediately in the UI:

curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/orders \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"orderId":"DEMOPLACE02","sku":"WIDGET-A","qty":2,"amount":149.5}'
localhost:4200/orders/DEMOPLACE02
moments after submission
localhost:4200/orders/DEMOPLACE02
~2.5s later, on refresh — Placed
Step 8

Watching a fresh order get cancelled and undone, live

Same idea, this time engineered to fail at CHARGE_PAYMENT:

curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/orders \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"orderId":"DEMOCANCEL02","sku":"WIDGET-A","qty":1,"amount":49.0,"failAt":"CHARGE_PAYMENT"}'
localhost:4200/orders/DEMOCANCEL02
moments after submission
localhost:4200/orders/DEMOCANCEL02
~2.5s later, on refresh — Cancelled, undo steps done

The full walkthrough, in one take

  • 00:00 order list, all statuses
  • — filter to Placed → open ORD002498
  • — Mark Shipped
  • — filter to Cancelled → open ORD002499
  • — filter to Needs attention → open ORD001911
  • — condition cleared → Retry compensation
  • — submit DEMOPLACE02 live → watch it reach Placed
  • — submit DEMOCANCEL02 live → watch it reach Cancelled
  • — back to list, page 2

Tests for the key behavior

services/coordinator/test/saga.e2e-spec.ts covers exactly the required scenarios, plus two more:

  • all steps succeed → order is Placed with all 4 DO steps DONE and no UNDO rows
  • a step fails → completed steps are undone and the order ends Cancelled
  • never runs a saga twice for the same order, even under concurrent duplicate submissions
  • a stuck compensation is flagged Needs-attention, and Retry resolves it once the condition clears — this is the scenario Step 6 walks through by hand, and the one that exposed both bugs above
  • restart recovery: resumes a saga left mid-flight
npm install
cd services/coordinator
npm run test:e2e
Known issue, not yet root-caused: the e2e suite's own testcontainers-managed MySQL currently fails migrations with Invalid default value for 'created_at', separate from the application bugs above — the identical migration runs cleanly under the docker-compose MySQL used for this walkthrough. Worth a follow-up before relying on npm run test:e2e in CI.
